source.title: Video In-context Learning
source.authors: Wen-Tao Zhang; Junliang Guo; Tian-Yu He; Li Zhao; Linli Xu; Jiang Bian

record.tranche_reason: Studies how video imitation metrics vary with model parameter count, extending scaling analysis to video models. It does not measure language-model held-out cross-entropy or fit a power law.
record.gate_note: The scaling results are in Figure 3. Table 1 reports demonstration-type comparisons for the 1.1B model, not scaling-sweep results. The study does not report held-out cross-entropy, loss fits, or compute-optimal allocations.
record.test_reason: The study trains autoregressive video Transformers at 300M, 700M and 1.1B parameters. It reports downstream imitation metrics (probing accuracy, its gain over random demonstrations, PSNR, FID) at each size. This bears weakly on V6 in a new setting (video models). It reports no loss values, no power-law fit, no token or compute sweep and no extrapolation, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors state that video imitation capacity 'follows the scaling law': larger models give better visual quality, more informative representations and more precise demonstration control. This rests only on monotone trends across three sizes, with no power-law fit.
record.recipe_differences: Instead of fitting language-model held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute, the study compares video-imitation metrics across three model sizes; it reports trends rather than fitted scaling exponents.
record.problems: Only three parameter counts are evaluated, over a much narrower range than several orders of magnitude. The scaling results are presented in plots without uncertainty estimates, and no power-law fit or extrapolation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Visual-quality metrics in Figure 3 are not included because they do not measure the downstream-style semantic performance named in V6.

untested.parts: No held-out loss is reported against parameters, tokens or compute, and no power-law fit is made.
No fit on small runs is used to predict larger runs.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is studied; training tokens appear fixed (4096M).
Shape is varied only together with size (Table 7); there is no fixed-parameter comparison of shapes.
Video models are studied, but no loss curve or power-law form is fitted, so whether the same form holds in video is not shown.
Predictability (any fitted law or prediction) is not tested; only three sizes over less than one order of magnitude. Prediction from pretraining loss is not tested.
Fitting choices and departures from a power law are not examined.

missing.what: Visual-quality scaling: PSNR (about 12.67→12.96→13.06) and FID (26.33, 21.29, 21.95, order ambiguous in the extracted figure). FID at 1.1B (21.95, matching Table 1) may be worse than at 700M, i.e. non-monotone. These are downstream generation metrics and bear on V6.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is thin: three model sizes within about 4×, figure-only values, no uncertainty, and no loss or compute reporting. Training tokens per size are not clearly stated beyond the 1.1B run (4096M tokens, 15 epochs). There are internal inconsistencies: Table 2 gives P-Acc 38.5 versus 36.7 elsewhere, and the 1.1B gain is 7.45 in Figure 3c versus 8.4 implied by Table 1. Researchers should treat the V6 support as qualitative and setting-specific (video, not language).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of losses fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same fitted power-law form holds in video or other modalities and training regimes.
Prediction from pretraining loss and performance on downstream tasks beyond the video-imitation metrics tested here.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

relationships.condition: VidIT video Transformers at 300M/700M/1.1B; SSv2 in-class demonstrations; probing-accuracy metrics
relationships.reason: P-Acc (19.5→31.6→36.7) and its gain over random demonstrations (2.5→3.5→7.45) rise monotonically with size (r1–r6). These are three points only and no fit is made.
relationships.display_finding: Probing accuracy rises monotonically from 19.5 to 31.6 to 36.7, while its gain over random demonstrations increases from 2.5 to 3.5 to 7.45.
